title: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
everyday_terms: extra fingers and poor night vision
summary: Bardet-Biedl syndrome affects many parts of the body. Common features are sight loss that starts in childhood, extra fingers or toes, weight gain and kidney differences.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (one of many linked to it) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Bardet-Biedl syndrome. Features vary, even within one family. Care from several specialist teams helps with sight, kidneys, weight and learning.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Bardet-Biedl syndrome. Could I be a carrier?
Can Bardet-Biedl syndrome skip a generation?
What does a test for Bardet-Biedl syndrome involve?
card_summary: Affects sight, kidneys and other parts of the body. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Affects sight, kidneys and more; care from several specialists.
care: Eye, kidney and endocrinology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
